metric_rationale: For each subject, the metric asks whether the option favored by the highest-validity discriminating expert was selected on more than half of trials, assigning 0.5 for an exact tie. It then reports the prevalence of subjects showing that directional pattern. TTB predicts above-chance agreement because the first discriminating cue determines every choice, whereas tallying predicts below-chance agreement because every designed trial has the opposing option winning the cue tally. Thresholding at the subject level exploits this sign reversal while reducing sensitivity to individual beta and epsilon values and to binomial trial noise. The A/B-swapped pairs ensure that the result cannot be generated merely by a response-side preference.

This is first-discriminating-cue choice accuracy. Every designed pair has an exactly tied tally, so Tallying predicts a tightly estimated value of 0.5. Take The Best instead favors the option identified by the first differing feature and predicts substantially greater than 0.5 alignment except at its highest noise levels. Pooling all 96 trials keeps the per-subject sampling variance low, while the A/B-reversed pairs balance the favored response side and therefore prevent a generic A/B response bias from creating the contrast.
